speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have yellowish skin and eyes and are feeling agitated; could you tell me if you have any abdominal pain or fever? Have you been consuming alcohol or taking any new medications recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your high-risk sexual history and recent onset of jaundice with agitation, I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis A, B, and C Serology. REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Tests (AST, ALT, Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase).

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly elevated AST and ALT levels strongly suggest acute hepatocellular injury, and given your high-risk sexual history, acute Hepatitis B is a primary concern. Do you have any dark urine or pale stools, and have you experienced any nausea or vomiting?

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you have unprotected sexual contact with a new partner in the last six months, or have you noticed dark urine and pale stools? I also need to know if you are experiencing nausea, vomiting, or right upper quadrant pain.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the high-risk sexual behavior and markedly elevated liver enzymes, acute Hepatitis B is the most likely diagnosis. I will proceed with a final targeted test to confirm this suspicion. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg).

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Hepatitis B is ruled out, I need to investigate other causes of acute hepatitis, particularly Hepatitis A or C given your social history. Have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or right upper quadrant abdominal pain recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the agitation and jaundice with normal HBsAg, I need to rule out Hepatitis C or other causes. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis C Antibody and RNA. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis A IgM.

speaker: Doctor
text: With viral hepatitis A, B, and C ruled out, I suspect acetaminophen toxicity or another drug-induced liver injury given the cocaine use. Did you take any over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen recently, and have you had any recent trauma or muscle injuries?

speaker: Doctor
text: The markedly elevated AST and ALT with jaundice, agitation, and negative viral hepatitis workup in a young male with a history of cocaine and ecstasy use strongly points to acute liver failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis or toxic hepatitis from recreational drug use. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatic Failure secondary to Recreational Drug Use (likely Rhabdomyolysis or Toxic Hepatitis)
